summary: All four production owner-proof readers now build GitHubApiClient with new SystemClock() instead of inline Date.now clocks, so hostedExecutionWait no longer rejects them as custom clocks when the bounded metadata reread is entered. The new regression test forces the first healthy jobs response to omit the runtime step for both future recovery and owner supersession, then asserts one 10s wait, a second jobs read, issued authority and zero state patches.

evidence: src/host/owner-install-future-recovery.ts, src/host/owner-install-supersession.ts (both readers), src/host/owner-install-supersession-normal.ts and src/host/owner-successor-acceptance-proof.ts replace inline real clocks with new SystemClock(), which the instanceof SystemClock branch in hostedExecutionWait accepts.

tests/host/owner-proof-metadata-delay_test.ts strips jobs[0].steps on the first healthy jobs read, advances the injected clock when the 10000ms metadata delay is scheduled, and asserts jobsReads equals 2, waits equals [10000], a defined authority and zero patches for the future recovery and owner supersession readers.

At the base commit the same readers passed plain clock objects without sleep, so the metadata-lag wait threw and readHostedExecution returned unavailable; the candidate change therefore removes the failure described by issue #312.
